front.title: MAP Payments: Negotiation, Settlement-Method Abstraction, Metering, and Disputes

abstract.t: Defines payment negotiation and evidence for MAP: quotes, agreements, invoices, settlement proofs, payment receipts, and a dispute-evidence protocol — over a registry of pluggable settlement methods (Lightning, card-processor intents, stablecoins, ACH, Interledger, private credit ledgers). MAP mandates no currency, token, chain, or processor; it standardizes how parties agree on price, prove settlement occurred on the chosen rail, and exchange evidence when they disagree. This replaces the orchestrator-minted-credit designs rejected in the critique (C9).

section.name: Requirements Language
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document family are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here. No adaptation or weakening of these terms applies.

section.name: Model and data semantics
section.t: Money moves on an external settlement rail; MAP moves signed statements about that movement. Ownership is explicit:

ul.li: The rail is the sole source of truth for whether value moved. MAP

section.t: proofs are pointers into the rail's truth, verifiable under the method's own rules.

ul.li: Each party owns its local payment-state view; there is no shared

section.t: payment state machine, no distributed transaction spanning rail and task, and no exactly-once assumption about rail operations — rails duplicate, delay, and fail-after-success, and every flow below is retry-safe under those conditions.
is the durable cross-context fact linking work to money; both are append-only events, deduplicated by content address.

Distinguish three moments explicitly (never conflate them): agreed (PAY_AGREE exchanged), submitted (payer initiated on the rail), settled (proof verifies under the method). Delivery obligations key off settled or off negotiated credit terms — never off submitted.
Amounts: CBOR decimal fractions (tag 4, integer mantissa/exponent) plus an asset identifier — never floats (core §4.2).

section.name: Message flow
section.sourcecode: Requester(payer) Provider(payee) | ←------------- PAY_QUOTE ----------- | (solicited by OFFER, tasks §2) | -- PAY_AGREE {quote-id, method} ---→ | | ... task executes; usage-update chunks ... | ←------------- PAY_INVOICE --------- | (final or incremental) | pay on the rail (out of band) | | -- PAY_PROOF {invoice-id, proof} --→ | verify under method rules | ←------------- PAY_RECEIPT --------- | signed "settled" statement
section.t: Prepaid and escrowed variants reorder steps (§5.2); credit terms (pay-after, net-N) collapse INVOICE/PROOF to post-delivery.

section.name: Quotes and agreements
section.sourcecode:
PayQuote = { ; msg-type 0x0400 1 => bstr .size 16, ; quote-id 2 => uint, ; pricing model: 0 flat, 1 per-token ; (in/out rates), 2 per-second, ; 3 per-invocation 3 => { * uint => [Asset, Amount] }, ; rate table keyed by unit code ? 4 => [Asset, Amount], ; estimated / maximum total 5 => [+ MethodOffer], 6 => Timestamp, ; expiry ? 7 => uint, ; terms: 0 postpaid, 1 prepaid, ; 2 escrow, 3 metered-incremental ? 8 => ExtMap, ? 9 => bstr .size 32 ; task binding: TaskID (tasks §1) } MethodOffer = { 1 => tstr /*method URI, §5*/, 2 => bstr /*opaque params*/ }
PayAgree = { ; msg-type 0x0401 1 => bstr .size 16, ; quote-id (binds exact quote bytes 2 => Multihash, ; via quote-envelope digest) 3 => tstr, ; chosen method URI ? 4 => [Asset, Amount] ; authorized cap (hard ceiling) }
section.t: Rate-table unit codes (registry; Specification Required, ops §3):

Units price a SINGLE counted unit (per token, per millisecond — not per-1k), so every billed amount is an exact uint counter × Amount product: no rounding rule exists anywhere in this document, by construction. Same-exponent rule: all Amounts in one quote's rate table MUST share one decimal exponent and MUST be in one Asset; cumulative-billed and invoice amounts derived from them carry that same exponent, so verifiers compare mantissas directly (an exponent mismatch is a rejection, never a conversion).

A signed PAY_AGREE referencing the quote digest is the enforceable agreement both sides hold; ASSIGN carries its reference (tasks §2.1). Quotes are binding until expiry (unlike descriptor PricingHints, which are advertisements only). The authorized cap is a hard constraint: usage beyond it without a fresh agreement is unbillable — the requester-side runaway-cost defense.

Task binding (key 9): when a PAY_QUOTE answers an OFFER that carries a TaskID (tasks §2), key 9 MUST be present and equal that TaskID, and the requester MUST treat a mismatching or absent binding as a quote for a different task (reject or re-quote). Quotes without key 9 are standing quotes: they MAY be agreed to and then bound to a task only via the ASSIGN's PayAgreeRef. This closes quote replay across tasks; replay of the quote bytes themselves is already excluded by the envelope msg-id and the PAY_AGREE digest binding.

section.name: Payment references (exported reference types)
section.t: Other documents refer to payment state by identity only (ops §2). The following types are the canonical cross-context references; digests are computed over the received envelope bytes of the referenced message (core invariant I1 — never over a re-serialization):
section.sourcecode: PayQuoteRef = { ; reference to a PAY_QUOTE 1 => bstr .size 16, ; quote-id 2 => Multihash ; digest of received PAY_QUOTE envelope } PayAgreeRef = { ; reference to a PAY_AGREE 1 => bstr .size 16, ; quote-id 2 => Multihash ; digest of received PAY_AGREE envelope } PayRef = { ; pre-quote pricing expectation (OFFER) ? 1 => uint, ; acceptable pricing model (as PayQuote.2) ? 2 => [Asset, Amount], ; maximum acceptable total ? 3 => [+ tstr], ; acceptable settlement method URIs (§5) ? 4 => PayAgreeRef ; standing agreement to price under } ; at least one member MUST be present
section.t: Quote.2 (tasks §2) is a PayQuoteRef; Assign.6 (tasks §2.1) is a PayAgreeRef; Offer.4 (tasks §2) is a PayRef. A PayRef is an expectation, not a commitment: a provider MAY quote outside it, and the requester's remedy is simply not to agree.

section.name: Metering and incremental settlement
section.t: For streaming work, usage-update chunks (tasks §3, kind 3) carry running {tokens-in, tokens-out, ms}. Under terms 3 (metered-incremental) the provider MAY issue incremental PAY_INVOICEs at usage watermarks; the requester tops up with PAY_PROOFs. If credit is exhausted, the provider pauses the stream with ERROR 6001 (retryable) and a final unpaid watermark; the requester either pays or CANCELs, owing usage to the last countersigned checkpoint (tasks §11) — the checkpoint is what makes "pay for what was delivered" well-defined for both sides. The exact pause/resume/cancel mechanics (no new message type; resume is the covering PAY_PROOF) are §4.2. Invoices are idempotent by invoice-id: re-sending an invoice or a proof MUST NOT double-bill or double-settle (receivers dedup; rails are consulted by proof, not by count).
section.sourcecode:
PayInvoice = { 1 => bstr .size 16 /*invoice-id*/, 2 => bstr /*quote-id*/, 3 => [Asset, Amount], ? 4 => UsageWatermark, 5 => bstr /*method payload: e.g. BOLT12 offer, processor intent id*/, 6 => Timestamp, ? 7 => uint /*escrow phase, terms 2 only: 1 hold, 2 release — §5.2.1*/ } PayProof = { 1 => bstr /*invoice-id*/, 2 => tstr /*method*/, 3 => bstr /*proof payload: preimage, intent confirmation, tx ref*/ } PayReceipt = { 1 => bstr /*invoice-id*/, 2 => [Asset, Amount], 3 => Timestamp, ? 4 => Multihash /*proof digest*/, ? 5 => uint /*kind: 0 settled (default), 1 held, 2 released, 3 refunded — §5.2.1; unknown values MUST be rejected*/ }
UsageWatermark = { ; PayInvoice key 4 (terms 3 only) 1 => TaskID, ; the metered task this invoice bills 2 => uint, ; through-chunk-seq: highest chunk-seq ; covered by this invoice (inclusive) 3 => Usage, ; CUMULATIVE usage since task start at ; that point (tasks §4 Complete key 4 ; shape: {1 tokens-in, 2 tokens-out, ; 3 ttft-ms, 4 wall-ms}) 4 => [Asset, Amount] ; cumulative-billed: total billed } ; through and including THIS invoice

section.name: Watermark semantics and verification
section.t: A watermark is cumulative since task start, never a delta: a re-sent invoice is byte-identical (idempotency falls out), each invoice is independently verifiable, and monotonicity is a component-wise >=. All four keys are REQUIRED when the watermark is present. Under terms 3 (metered-incremental) every PAY_INVOICE MUST carry key 4; under any other terms key 4 MUST be absent.
cumulative-billed (key 4) MUST equal the agreed rate table applied to the cumulative usage (key 3) under the agreed pricing model (§3):

ul.li: model 2 (per-second): wall-ms × rate[3] (rate unit 3 is per

section.t: MILLISECOND — §3 unit codes — so the product is exact)

All products are exact (uint counter × decimal-fraction rate under the §3 same-exponent rule); no rounding is defined or permitted. The invoice amount (key 3) MUST equal this invoice's cumulative-billed minus the cumulative-billed of the last invoice the requester settled for this task (zero for the first).
The requester MUST verify, in order, before paying:

ol.li: monotonicity: through-chunk-seq, every Usage component, and

A rejected invoice is not settled and does not advance the accepted watermark.

section.name: Pause, resume, and cancel
section.t: Metered settlement introduces no new message type: pause, resume, and cancel are expressed entirely with messages already defined (ERROR, PAY_PROOF, FLOW_CREDIT, CANCEL). The exhaustion signal is proof absence, exactly as in the postpaid flow — a requester that cannot or will not pay an invoice simply withholds its PAY_PROOF; there is no "insufficient" message.

Pause is a provider-local decision, not a wire handshake. A provider MAY pause the stream whenever it holds an unpaid outstanding watermark (billed minus settled), and it SIGNALS the pause with ERROR 6001 (retryable) whose detail map (core §9 key 5) carries the final unpaid watermark as {1 => UsageWatermark}. RECOMMENDED policy: pause when the unpaid amount would exceed the stream's granted flow credit (core §8.1) or the provider's own per-stream exposure limit — so that unpaid delivery is bounded by exactly the backpressure MAP already provides. While paused, the provider MUST NOT emit further billable CHUNKs, MUST NOT re-issue a new invoice-id for already-billed usage (the paused invoice stands, idempotent by id — the 6001 watermark merely restates the outstanding position so a requester that missed the invoice can reconstruct it), and MUST NOT advance the watermark.

Resume requires no marker: the covering PAY_PROOF IS the resume trigger. When the provider observes a PAY_PROOF that settles the outstanding invoice(s) which caused the pause, it settles (PAY_RECEIPT) and continues streaming from the exact watermark — no gap and no double-bill, since the watermark is cumulative and monotonic. The next CHUNK the requester receives is itself the observable resume. A metered stream also remains governed by FLOW_CREDIT throughout: a requester that wishes to stop receiving (and thus being billed) MAY simply stop granting credit, starving the stream through the existing core §8.1 mechanism.

Cancel: on CANCEL (tasks §2, msg-type 0x020C) instead of top-up, the amount owed anchors to the last countersigned checkpoint (tasks §8.2 key 5 usage, billed under the same §4.1 formula), which both sides hold signed — never to an unpaid watermark the requester never countersigned. The owed amount is therefore always ≤ the final unpaid watermark: a dying or malicious stream can claim payment only for delivery the requester has already acknowledged at a checkpoint.

PAY_RECEIPT is the payee's signed past-tense fact "this invoice settled"; it feeds ExecutionReceipt.payment-ref and is the payer's permanent proof of payment independent of rail-side record retention.

section.name: Registry (Specification Required; initial entries)

tr.td: intent id + processor confirmation fetchable by payee
x402 (HTTP-native stablecoin; EIP-3009 authorizations, facilitator settle)
signed transfer authorization; settled = facilitator/chain settlement

section.t: Each entry's defining document specifies: params schema, proof schema, verification procedure, finality/reversal model, and refund reference format. Reversibility is a method property the payee prices in (an ACH "settled" can still reverse; a preimage cannot) — MAP surfaces it, never hides it.

Method definition — pay:credit-ledger (added 2026-07-06 from TASK-009). A named ledger operator (a mesh-configured AgentID, trusted BY DESIGN for this method — the payee prices that trust in). Params (MethodOffer.2): none required for the MVP. Proof payload (PayProof.3): CBOR [entry-bytes, sig] where
section.sourcecode: entry-bytes = enc(["MAPLedgerEntry", invoice-id, payer-AgentID, payee-AgentID, [Asset, Amount], ts]) sig = Ed25519 by the operator over entry-bytes
section.t: Verification (payee): verify_strict sig against the operator AgentID, then the entry's invoice-id / payer / payee / [Asset, Amount] MUST equal the invoice being settled. Finality: instant and irreversible within the ledger (no chargeback path); balances move exactly once per invoice-id (operator dedups). Refund reference: a fresh entry in the reverse direction (out of MVP scope).

Method definition — pay:x402 (added 2026-07-14, ARCHITECT DESIGN; see CHANGELOG). Settles via the x402 protocol (x402.org, Apache-2.0): the payer signs an exact-amount, time-boxed, single-use on-chain transfer authorization (EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization for EVM stablecoins such as USDC) and the payee — directly or through a payee-chosen facilitator service's /verify and /settle endpoints — executes it on chain. MAP adopts x402's settlement payload and facilitator model only: x402's own HTTP 402/X-PAYMENT request loop is NOT used between MAP peers (PAY_QUOTE / PAY_AGREE / PAY_INVOICE already carry the negotiation with stronger binding); it remains appropriate at a gateway (ops §5) that fronts external x402-priced HTTP services as MAP capabilities.

Asset/amount mapping: the quote's Asset MUST be the erc20:<chain>:<addr> form (§1) naming the token the scheme settles, and the Amount exponent MUST be the token's decimals negated (USDC ⇒ −6), so the mantissa IS the atomic unit count — the §3 exact-arithmetic rules apply unchanged.
Params (MethodOffer.2, deterministic-CBOR map):
section.sourcecode: X402Params = { 1 => uint, ; x402Version (1 in this revision) 2 => tstr, ; scheme ("exact" in this revision) 3 => tstr, ; network id (e.g. "base", "base-sepolia") 4 => tstr, ; payTo: payee on-chain address ? 5 => tstr, ; facilitator base URL (informative — payee's choice) ? 6 => uint ; max authorization validity the payee accepts (s) }
section.t: Proof payload (PayProof.3, deterministic-CBOR map):

Invoice binding (MAP-specific MUST): the authorization's 32-byte nonce MUST be SHA-256("MAP-x402-nonce" || invoice-id); the payee MUST verify it. This binds the authorization to exactly one MAP invoice, and the chain's single-use-nonce rule then enforces exactly-once settlement across retries (layered under MAP's invoice-id idempotency, not replacing it).

Verification (payee): decode the payload; check x402Version/scheme/network/ payTo against the offered params, the token contract against the quote's Asset, value == the invoice Amount mantissa (atomic units), the nonce rule above, and a validity window covering now + expected settle latency; then settle (facilitator /settle or direct submission). A successful /verify alone is NOT settlement — the payee MUST NOT reply PAY_RECEIPT (or release anything priced) before the settlement succeeds/confirms per its params. Finality: reversal-resistant once the transfer confirms; the facilitator is a payee-chosen, payee-trusted intermediary (the payer's exposure is bounded by the exact-amount, time-boxed, single-use authorization) — reversibility and facilitator trust are method properties the payee prices in, per this section's doctrine. Refund reference: the tx hash of a reverse transfer (out of MVP scope).

section.name: Prepay and escrow (terms 1 and 2)
section.t: Both variants move settlement BEFORE delivery. Neither adds a message type (the same doctrine as §4.2): they are reorderings of the §2 flow plus two additive optional fields — the invoice phase and the receipt kind (§5.2.1). What they demand of the rail differs: prepay needs nothing beyond §5.1; escrow is a method capability — only methods that support conditional holds (hold-invoice Lightning, processor auth-then-capture, contract escrow, the §5.2.4 credit-ledger extension) may be offered in a terms-2 quote, and including a MethodOffer in a terms-2 quote asserts that the offered instance supports it. MAP's role is unchanged in kind: the rail holds and moves the money; MAP defines the signed statements, their ordering, and the canonical release trigger both parties can evaluate — COMPLETE + verified transcript-root (tasks §4).

A quote under terms 1 or 2 MUST carry key 4 (estimated/maximum total): it is the amount settled or held up front, under the §3 same-exponent rule. Terms are exclusive; combined metered-escrow (a held ceiling drawn down by watermarks) is not defined in this revision.

section.name: Receipt kinds and invoice phases (additive fields)
section.t: PayReceipt key 5 kind: 0 settled (the default when absent — all pre-existing receipts are unchanged), 1 held, 2 released, 3 refunded. Receivers MUST reject a receipt with an unrecognized kind (fail-closed; ERROR 6010). Only kinds 0 and 2 are settlement statements and feed ExecutionReceipt.payment-ref; kind 1 is the payee's signed statement that a conforming hold exists on the rail; kind 3 records a return of held funds to the payer.

PayInvoice key 7 phase: 1 hold, 2 release. Key 7 MUST be present iff the governing agreement's terms are 2 (the mirror of the §4.1 watermark presence rule); a violation is ERROR 6010 (escrow violation, core §9).

section.name: Terms 1 — prepaid
section.sourcecode: Requester(payer) Provider(payee) | ←---- PAY_QUOTE {terms 1} ---------- | | -- PAY_AGREE ----------------------→ | | ←---- PAY_INVOICE ------------------ | amount = quote key 4 total | pay on the rail (out of band) | | -- PAY_PROOF ----------------------→ | verify under method rules | ←---- PAY_RECEIPT {settled} -------- | | ... task executes ... | | ←------------- COMPLETE ------------ |
section.t: Rules: the single PAY_INVOICE MUST equal the quote's key 4 total and carries no watermark (§4.1) and no phase key (§5.2.1). The provider MUST NOT begin billable execution before the invoice is settled — delivery keys off settled (§1), which is precisely what the payer buys with a prepay. An amount other than the quoted total is ERROR 6010. Excess of prepay over eventual usage is not overbilling (the payer agreed the total; dispute claim 3 does not apply); non-delivery after settlement is dispute claim 0, with the receipt and the absent COMPLETE as evidence, remedied by the method's refund reference or the mesh's §6 process.

section.name: Terms 2 — escrow
section.t: Escrow adds a fourth moment to §1's three: held — value locked on the rail such that the payer cannot unilaterally reclaim it, the payee cannot unilaterally claim it, and a defined expiry returns it to the payer. Under terms 2, delivery obligations key off held; final settlement keys off released.
section.sourcecode: Requester(payer) Provider(payee) | ←---- PAY_QUOTE {terms 2} ---------- | | -- PAY_AGREE ----------------------→ | | ←---- PAY_INVOICE {phase 1 hold} --- | amount = quote key 4 total | place hold on the rail (oob) | | -- PAY_PROOF {hold proof} ---------→ | verify hold under method | ←---- PAY_RECEIPT {kind 1 held} ---- | | ... task executes ... | | ←------------- COMPLETE ------------ | transcript-root (tasks §4) | verify COMPLETE + transcript-root | | ←---- PAY_INVOICE {phase 2 release}- | amount = final owed ≤ held | authorize release on the rail (oob)| | -- PAY_PROOF {release proof} ------→ | | ←---- PAY_RECEIPT {kind 2 released}- | remainder refunds to payer
section.t: Escrow is two invoice rounds, each the standard invoice→proof→receipt unit: hold and release carry distinct invoice-ids, both bound to the same quote-id, and §4's idempotency rules apply per round unchanged (a re-sent hold or release invoice is byte-identical; a re-delivered proof settles nothing twice).
The requester MUST verify, in order, before acting on a terms-2 invoice:

ol.li: phase: key 7 present and ∈ {1, 2}, per §5.2.1 — else ERROR 6010;
hold invoices: amount equals the quote key 4 total, and no prior hold

section.t: exists for this agreement (one hold per agreement) — else 6010;

ol.li: release invoices: a COMPLETE for the bound task has been received AND

section.t: its transcript-root verified (tasks §4) — the canonical release trigger. A release invoice before that MUST NOT be paid: 6010;

ol.li: release amount: ≤ the held amount; and if the task ended by CANCEL,

section.t: exactly the §4.1 formula applied to the last countersigned checkpoint's usage (the §4.2 cancel anchor) — else 6010;

Authorization symmetry (the property that makes a hold an escrow and not a transfer): the rail/operator MUST NOT move held funds to the payee without a payer-signed release authorization bound to (hold-invoice-id, release-invoice-id, amount) — the payee cannot self-release; and held funds MUST NOT return to the payer before expiry without a payee-signed refund authorization — the payer cannot unwind a hold it granted. At release, the remainder (held minus released) returns to the payer in the same rail operation. A payer that verifies COMPLETE and then withholds its release signature is dispute claim 2 (non-payment), with the kind-1 receipt, the signed COMPLETE, and the transcript as evidence — MAP makes the lie expensive to sustain (§6); the method and mesh make it remediable.

Expiry: every hold MUST carry an expiry (method params); at expiry, unreleased funds return to the payer in full, and a release fails on the rail thereafter (ERROR 6002 at the MAP layer). Payees SHOULD price the expiry at deadline + expected release latency with margin — an expiry shorter than the task deadline is self-harm, not a protocol violation.

Failure matrix (honest-party exposure is bounded in every row): COMPLETE never arrives → expiry refunds the payer (dispute claim 0 if a record matters); CANCEL → release invoice for the checkpoint-anchored amount, remainder refunded (a kind-3 receipt for the remainder is OPTIONAL); provider vanishes → expiry refund; payer vanishes after COMPLETE → dispute claim 2, and the payee's loss is bounded by work it can prove it delivered. The payee's exposure is bounded by the hold (it never works beyond held value); the payer's by the expiry (money returns absent its own signature).

section.name: `pay:credit-ledger` escrow extension
section.t: The §5.1 credit-ledger method supports terms 2 with three additional operator-signed entry forms (same [entry-bytes, sig] proof envelope and verification rules as §5.1). Params (MethodOffer.2) under terms 2: {? 1 => uint} — maximum hold validity the operator accepts, seconds.
section.sourcecode: hold-entry = enc(["MAPLedgerHold", hold-invoice-id, payer, payee, [Asset, Amount], expiry-ts, ts]) release-auth = enc(["MAPLedgerReleaseAuth", hold-invoice-id, release-invoice-id, [Asset, Amount]]) ; signed by the PAYER, presented to the operator refund-auth = enc(["MAPLedgerRefundAuth", hold-invoice-id]) ; signed by the PAYEE (pre-expiry refund) release-entry = enc(["MAPLedgerRelease", hold-invoice-id, release-invoice-id, payer, payee, [Asset, Amount], ts]) refund-entry = enc(["MAPLedgerRefund", hold-invoice-id, payer, [Asset, Amount], ts])
section.t: Operator rules: a hold moves Amount from the payer's balance into an escrow bucket keyed by hold-invoice-id (idempotent by that id; insufficient balance → no entry). A release requires a valid payer release-auth over exactly this (hold, release, amount) triple, amount ≤ held, and now < expiry; it atomically credits the amount to the payee, returns the remainder to the payer, and closes the hold (idempotent by release-invoice-id). A refund requires expiry passed OR a valid payee refund-auth, returns the held amount to the payer, and closes the hold. The hold entry is the PAY_PROOF payload for the phase-1 invoice; the release entry for the phase-2 invoice.

pay:credit-ledger deliberately accommodates community meshes running reputation-priced barter or operator-run tabs — with the ledger operator named and chosen, not smuggled in as protocol (the fix for C9's accidental central bank).

section.name: Disputes
section.t: Scope: MAP adjudicates evidence availability, not outcomes. The protocol's whole job here is that each party can (a) state a precise claim bound to a precise agreement, (b) hand over the signed artifacts that bear on it, and (c) let ANY third party the disputants choose (mesh arbiter, method-level chargeback, court) check the claim mechanically without trusting either disputant. Timeboxes, arbiter selection, and remedies are mesh/method policy — deliberately outside this document. Design goal: make lying expensive to sustain — every step of a MAP payment leaves a signed artifact the liar must contradict.

section.name: Messages
section.t: Unrecognized claim codes and evidence kinds MUST be rejected (fail-closed). Disputes are idempotent by dispute-id; re-sent evidence messages MUST NOT duplicate items in the verifier's view (dedup by item content address). Opening a dispute does not suspend other machinery by itself; a party refusing to continue a flow pending resolution signals ERROR 6003 (dispute opened). A receipt with outcome 4 (disputed, trust §3) records the event on the trust plane either way, whoever proves right.

section.name: Third-party verifiability and CB disclosure
section.t: Inner-signed artifacts (ExecutionReceipts, checkpoint countersignatures — decision-9-style signatures over stated bytes) are verifiable by anyone from the bytes alone. Envelope artifacts are COSE_Sign1 over the received bytes with external_aad = the session channel binding (CB) when sent in-session (core §7.3) — so a third party CANNOT verify them without the CB. Therefore: an EvidenceItem carrying an in-session envelope MUST include key 3 (the CB value); out-of-session envelopes (empty external_aad) omit it. Disclosing a CB post-hoc is safe — it is an HKDF output, not key material, and reveals nothing about session traffic keys — and it is useful: all in-session items verifying under the SAME disclosed CB are thereby proven to come from one session between the two disputants. A verifier MUST treat an in-session item whose CB is absent or fails verification as unavailable evidence, not as a verified artifact.

section.name: Mechanical verification procedure
section.t: Given a PayDispute and both parties' evidence sets, a verifier (either disputant, or any third party) proceeds: authenticate every item per §6.2 against the AgentIDs bound by the agreement (item signers MUST be the disputants or the method's named operator; anything else is discarded); resolve the agreement (kind-1 item matching PayAgreeRef's digest, and its kind-0 quote matching the agreement's quote digest — the 6006 machinery); then evaluate the claim:

ul.li: 0 non-delivery (payer claims): supported iff the payer's evidence

section.t: shows value moved — a settled PAY_RECEIPT (kind 0/2) or verified proof — AND the payee's evidence contains NO countersigned checkpoint and no COMPLETE for the bound task. This is rebuttal-shaped: absence is never proven, so the claim stands unrebutted if the payee, who by construction holds the countersigned artifacts if delivery happened, produces none.

ul.li: 1 output-mismatch (payer claims): supported iff the COMPLETE's

section.t: transcript-root does not equal the root recomputed (tasks §8.1) over the delivered transcript the payer presents, at or before the COMPLETE's chunk range. Fully mechanical.

ul.li: 2 non-payment (payee claims): rebuttal-shaped dual of claim 0:

section.t: stands unless the payer produces a verifying PAY_PROOF / receipt / release-auth covering the invoice (escrow: the release round).

ul.li: 3 overbilling (payer claims): supported iff an invoice's

section.t: cumulative-billed (or a terms-1/2 amount) exceeds the §4.1 formula applied to the highest COUNTERSIGNED usage (checkpoint key 5) in evidence, under the agreement's rate table — exact arithmetic, no tolerance. (Watermarks the payer accepted but did not countersign bill validly under §4.1; overbilling is measured against what the payer ACKNOWLEDGED, which is why checkpoints exist.)

ul.li: 4 terms breach (either): supported iff the evidence itself

section.t: exhibits a violation of §3–§5.2 rules that existing verifiers detect mechanically: quote-digest mismatch (6006), cap breach (6005), watermark violation (6009), escrow-phase/prepaid violation (6010), invalid proof (6008). The claim names the rule; the verifier re-runs the corresponding check over the presented artifacts.

The verdict vocabulary is three-valued: supported, rebutted, or insufficient evidence — MAP never emits remedies. Both rebuttal-shaped claims (0, 2) resolve against the party that withholds artifacts it must hold if honest; that asymmetry is the availability doctrine doing its work.

section.name: Griefing bounds
section.t: A dispute is itself a signed artifact: frivolous disputants accumulate their own evidence trail (§7), and outcome-4 receipts weigh against both parties' trust projections pending resolution (trust §5). Evidence volume rides FLOW_CREDIT (§6.1 more chunking) — a party cannot flood; a verifier MAY cap total evidence size as local policy and rule "insufficient" beyond it.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: Proof replay: proofs bind to invoice-ids; invoice-ids bind to quote digests; core replay rules (§7) cover the envelopes — a captured proof re-settles nothing. Price-switch: quotes are bound by digest in PAY_AGREE, so a payee cannot substitute terms. Griefing via disputes: disputes are signed and receiptable; frivolous disputants accumulate their own evidence trail. Sanctions/AML/KYC obligations attach to settlement methods and their operators, not to the negotiation layer; gateways and method implementations MUST NOT be assumed compliance-free (ops §9). Metadata: invoices reveal counterparties and amounts to rail operators per the chosen method — surface this in method definitions so zone policy can exclude rails inconsistent with the task's sensitivity.

section.name: IANA-Style Considerations
section.t: Registers: settlement method URIs (Specification Required); pricing model codes; terms codes; dispute claim codes; dispute evidence-item kinds (§6.1); unit codes for rate tables. The assigned values and the family-wide index are in draft-map-wire-01.md §3.18, §3.19, and §3.20; in case of divergence the normative definitions in §3, §5.1, and §6 govern.
